candidate_sentence_map.S1: Tallinna Sadam reported a stronger overall performance in 2025 despite slightly lower revenue.
candidate_sentence_map.S2: Revenue decreased 0.8% to EUR 118.7 million, mainly because icebreaker Botnica charter fees fell by EUR 4.0 million, or 34%, as charter days declined by 42.
candidate_sentence_map.S3: This was partly offset by higher vessel dues, passenger fees, lease income, ferry-service revenue and cargo charges.
candidate_sentence_map.S4: Vessel dues increased 8% to EUR 34.1 million, while ferry-service revenue rose 1% to EUR 36.4 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S5: Profitability improved materially as operating expenses related to the main operations declined by EUR 3.8 million, or 4%, to EUR 88.0 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S6: Operating expenses alone fell 10%, primarily due to lower maintenance and repair costs, reduced fuel and lease expenses, and a EUR 0.9 million insurance indemnity related to the 2024 Botnica technical failure.
candidate_sentence_map.S7: Adjusted EBITDA increased 6.4% to EUR 56.5 million, lifting the margin from 44.4% to 47.6%.
candidate_sentence_map.S8: Operating profit rose 12.2% to EUR 32.7 million, and the operating margin improved from 24.4% to 27.6%.
candidate_sentence_map.S9: Profit before income tax increased 25% to EUR 27.9 million, supported by a EUR 2.5 million reduction in net finance costs as interest rates and debt declined.
candidate_sentence_map.S10: Net profit rose 17.3% to EUR 22.5 million, with earnings per share increasing from EUR 0.07 to EUR 0.09.
candidate_sentence_map.S11: The increase in income tax expense, up 73.3% to EUR 5.4 million following changes to dividend taxation, limited the growth in net profit.
candidate_sentence_map.S12: The associate Green Marine contributed a EUR 26 thousand loss, compared with a EUR 487 thousand profit in 2024.
candidate_sentence_map.S14: Cargo volume increased 5.1% to 13.8 million tonnes, driven especially by a 47% increase in liquid bulk and moderate growth in dry bulk.
candidate_sentence_map.S15: Passenger numbers rose 1.0% to 8.3 million, including a 25% increase in cruise passengers; however, volumes remained approximately 78% of the pre-pandemic level.
candidate_sentence_map.S16: Domestic ferry traffic served 2.5 million passengers and 1.2 million vehicles, while Botnica’s utilisation rate fell to 49%.
candidate_sentence_map.S17: Capital investment decreased 14.4% to EUR 33.2 million, with major spending on the new multifunctional quay at Paldiski South Harbour, Muuga quay reinforcement and ferry maintenance.
candidate_sentence_map.S18: Net debt declined 15.5% to EUR 141.7 million, and operating cash flow increased to EUR 53.7 million from EUR 48.7 million.
candidate_sentence_map.S19: The Group paid EUR 19.2 million in dividends, or EUR 0.073 per share.
candidate_sentence_map.S20: Management expects moderate passenger and cargo growth in 2026 but anticipates pressure from higher input costs, increased financing needs and the absence of certain one-off benefits, potentially reducing operating and net profit.
